The whole app re-tints from the pet's photo and plays like a tiny care game: a pixel room on Home, a sticker album, quests with XP and a HUD-style day recap.

background, surfaces, outlines, text and accent are all derived from the snapped preset (light and dark), and every text pair is checked to ≥ 4.5:1 — the pet's color is everywhere, not just on buttons.
Fredoka + Nunito, a pixel font only for HUD numbers, 2px ink outlines, hard “sticker” shadows and bouncy press states (motion turns off with reduced-motion).
the photo is pixelated live into a sprite that lives in a room and reacts to mood — night window when sleepy, empty bowl when hungry — with Joy / Food / Energy meters.
an album grid with sticker stamps instead of a timeline; tap a photo for the AI caption.
meds, walk and meals become quests; Done fills the day's XP bar with a little burst. In the real app Chloe taps Done with a photo — the owner just watches it fill.
stat cards, a mood timeline and a short AI note from Chloe that fill in live as quests clear.
Meds and meals become quests with XP. Does that feel motivating, or too light for an anxious owner?
